items.title: Iran's Hardliners Push For Nuclear Weapons As U.S. War Drags On
items.content_text:
Iran's Hardliners Push For Nuclear Weapons As U.S. War Drags On

Authored by RFE/RL Staff via OilPrice,

It was once taboo in Iran to publicly speak about developing nuclear weapons. The authorities would often point to former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's religious edict barring the development of weapons of mass destruction. Iranian officials have long insisted the country's nuclear program is solely for civilian purposes.

Open calls for a bomb from sitting lawmakers and senior security officials would have been unthinkable a few years ago. But with the war with the United States in limbo, that's no longer the case.

After almost eight months of conflict and with Washington reportedly weighing strikes on Pickaxe Mountain, a deep underground site where US and Israeli officials say Iran has moved thousands of centrifuges, the talk is even growing.

Kamal Kharazi, an adviser to Khamenei who was killed in Israeli strikes earlier this year, said in 2024 that Tehran "might review our nuclear doctrine" if it felt an existential threat. The US-Israeli war against Iran this year seems to be seen by some as that very existential threat.

Khamenei and a cadre of Iran's top security and military brass were killed in the opening salvo of the war on February 28. While the strikes mostly targeted sites affiliated with the state, the military, or nuclear facilities, civilian infrastructure was also hit and ordinary Iranians killed.

Major US military operations have wound down in favor of economic pressure, including a naval blockade of Iranian ports, and indirect talks through mediators have stalled.

US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's recent proposal for a seven-day cease-fire and a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and he has threatened to resume major strikes. Washington says any deal must include what Vice President JD Vance called a "meaningful" reduction in Iran's uranium enrichment capacity.

Open Calls To Go Nuclear

Iran signed the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) in 1968 and ratified it in 1970. The NPT bars nuclear states from sharing arsenals and obliges non-nuclear states not to build them, while guaranteeing access to peaceful nuclear technology under safeguards.

It also signed the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) with a group of global powers, including the United States, in 2015 that limited Tehran's nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief.

But since Trump unilaterally pulled the United States out of the accord in 2018, Iran has ramped up its enrichment of uranium, though it continued to claim its nuclear program was purely for civilian purposes.

In June last year, Israel and the United States carried out air strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities, warning that Iran was close to developing nuclear weapons. On February 28, the two ramped up the pressure further by launching the air strikes that led to the current war.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a lawmaker and member of the parliament's influential National Security and Foreign Policy committee, recently argued that Iran has already paid a price for its nuclear program - and that it's time to produce weapons.

Hossein Ali Haji-Deligani, another lawmaker, described Iran's lack of nuclear deterrence as one of its major weaknesses and suggested a bomb could be tested in the not-too-distant future.

Even Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, suggested pursuing nukes is not off the table. He has blamed Trump's policies for "pushing the world toward acquiring nuclear weapons."

Davud Modarresian, a conservative commentator and proponent of going nuclear, wrote on X that developing a bomb is "more important than food."

He argued that developing a nuclear bomb would serve as "a guarantee of the country's survival," pointing to Trump's comment earlier this month about the importance of maintaining good relations with nuclear powers.

"When people have 11 nuclear missiles, it's nice to get along," Trump said about North Korea and his relations with its leader, Kim Jong Un.

In 2003, Khamenei officially issued a fatwa banning the development, possession, and use of nuclear weapons by Iran under Islamic law.

Modarresian said the fatwa has never really been an obstacle to developing nukes and blamed "indecision and lack of unified political will" for Iran not weaponizing its nuclear program.

But some, at least in public, have pushed back on weaponizing the nuclear program, or what's left of it.

Mohammad Mokhber, a former vice president who currently serves as a senior adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, said Iran already has the deterrence it needs. Speaking on October 19, he credited Tehran's policy of regionalizing the conflict as a strong enough deterrence.

Mokhber also played up Iran's ability to disrupt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, saying, "Any country that has the Strait of Hormuz has no need for an atomic bomb." He argued that controlling the chokepoint impacts billions of people whereas a bomb "might kill 50,000 to 100,000 people."

Meanwhile commentators opposed to developing nukes warn about the repercussions of attempting to acquire a bomb.

Sina Jahani, a journalist based in Tehran, argued that abandoning the NPT and producing a nuclear weapon would be "playing into Israel's hands."

Meanwhile, political commentator Amir Ali Abolfath cautioned that Iran's adversaries would learn of any moves to build nukes before Iran could produce them.

"What happens when the country's entire infrastructure is destroyed after a destructive American attack before nuclear deterrence is achieved?" he wrote on X, directing his question to proponents of going nuclear. "Would acquiring an atomic bomb after the destruction of the country still bring deterrence?"

State Of The Nuclear Program

As Iranians argue over whether to weaponize the nuclear program, a more practical question looms: Can Iran actually build a bomb, given the state of its nuclear infrastructure?

Iran's ability to enrich uranium has been crippled, but the core of its nuclear program likely survives.

Of the three enrichment plants, the only aboveground one, at Natanz, was destroyed. The other two, at Natanz and Fordow, were badly damaged and are widely believed to be out of action. Strikes also destroyed Iran's only uranium milling and conversion facilities.

The biggest unknown is the fate of Iran's 440.9 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60 percent purity. Rafael Grossi, director-general of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), said back in March that more than 200 kg of that stockpile remains in tunnels at Isfahan, with some at Natanz. The agency said in September that it had lost track of the stockpiles more than a year ago.

US and Israeli officials say Iran moved thousands of centrifuges into Pickaxe Mountain, buried an estimated 80-100 meters deep in granite. Trump last week said Washington "may have to go there."

In theory, as long as Iran is in possession of its highly enriched uranium stockpile, it can enrich it to weapons grade with little effort and just a few centrifuges, which is why the Pickaxe Mountain site has been in the news for a while. Whether it has the ability to produce a bomb, however, is a different matter.

Iran has long rejected the idea of giving up its stockpile but has offered to dilute it as part of a wider agreement with the United States to end the war, now in its eighth month.

items.title: "Even 1, 2, Or 3% Could Make The Difference": Trump Vows "Powerful Legal Options" To Purge Alaska's Other Dan Sullivan... Who Got 2.5%
items.content_text:
"Even 1, 2, Or 3% Could Make The Difference": Trump Vows "Powerful Legal Options" To Purge Alaska's Other Dan Sullivan... Who Got 2.5%

Most incumbents worry about their opponent. Dan Sullivan has to worry about his name (remember the two Dan Sullivan thing?).

Dan Sullivan (R) the incumbent: 

Dan Sullivan (R) the challenger: 

At Wednesday evening, a few hours after his South Carolina rally, President Trump took to Truth Social with a fresh grievance about Alaska's US Senate race, where Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan shares the ballot with a retired Petersburg schoolteacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. The post, in full, per the Newsweek write-up and an X mirror of Trump's posts:

"I am very concerned about the Dan S. Sullivan Race for the U.S. Senate in Alaska in that it is totally confusing, with the Dumocrats putting up another man, totally unrelated to Politics, named Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr. It's ridiculous that the Court didn't stop this SCAM. Even 1, 2, or 3% could make the difference. Dan S. Sullivan is leading by a lot, but this is CHEATING in an Election, and the Judge that allowed this to happen should be ashamed of himself. We are looking at powerful legal options to remove the fraudulent Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. from the Ballot, and holding the Democrats accountable for their Election Interference, in the pursuit of Justice and Fairness. President DONALD J. TRUMP"

The MAGA side of X took it from there:

🔥🚨 JUST IN - President Trump just flagged a major problem in the Alaska Senate race where Democrats put up a man named Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr. who has nothing to do with politics?

Trump called the situation totally confusing and said it is ridiculous that the Court did not... pic.twitter.com/qD2UtUUTeN

— The Patriot Oasis™ (@ThePatriotOasis) October 22, 2026

In other words, the president is promising to litigate a ballot that Alaska's courts have already ruled on, 12 days before the vote, over a candidate who couldn't crack 3%. Below we walk through who the "fraudulent" Sullivan actually is, what the courts said, and why "leading by a lot" and "1, 2, or 3% could make the difference" don't sit well in the same sentence.

Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. is a 69-year-old retired elementary-school teacher who has lived in Petersburg for 46 years and worked for the US Forest Service. He's not related to the senator. Here's where it gets interesting: he's a registered Republican, not a Democrat. He was a member of the Alaska Independence Party and registered as a Republican after that party dissolved late last year, per Newsweek. In June correspondence with state investigators he said he had had no contact with the campaign of Democrat Mary Peltola. He has denied being a plant, saying he entered the race out of frustration with the senator.

Alaska News adds that no Division of Elections record supports the claim that Democrats put him up. So the "Dumocrat" plant is a Republican. Brave.

The Courts Already Spoke

This isn't a new fight. Per Newsweek, Alaska's Division of Elections, overseen by Republican Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom, moved in June to remove him, concluding his candidacy was intended "to confuse or mislead and to thereby compromise the ballot's fairness or neutrality." A judge overturned that decision, and the Alaska Supreme Court ruled in late June that he could stay on the ballot. To tell the two apart, the ballot lists the incumbent as "Sullivan, Dan S." with an incumbent tag and the challenger as "Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.," and leaves the challenger's party line blank.

Under Alaska's top-four primary, he finished third on Aug. 18 with 2.47% (4,107 votes), per state results, which put him on the November ranked-choice ballot. Trump had already warned voters before the primary, calling him an "imposter" and urging Alaskans to "VOTE FOR THE REAL DAN SULLIVAN."

About that: The latest Data for Progress poll (Oct. 8-16) had Peltola 47%, Sullivan 44% on first choices, and 51-49 Peltola after ranked-choice reallocation. Rasmussen (Oct. 12-15) had Peltola 44-42. Averages put the Democrat up roughly 2-3.5 points.

items.title: Kushner Denies Bombshell Book Claims Of Secret Gulf-Funded Accounts
items.content_text:
Kushner Denies Bombshell Book Claims Of Secret Gulf-Funded Accounts

Jared Kushner is denying explosive allegations that, while serving as a senior White House adviser in Trump's first term, he had access to secret foreign bank accounts stocked with roughly $2 billion from Gulf royals - and that Dutch intelligence watched him use one of them through his hacked iPhone.

The claims come from an excerpt of investigative journalist Matthew Cole's forthcoming book Princes and Thieves, published Thursday by Vanity Fair. Cole alleges that Saudi and Emirati money funded a roughly $750 million account in the UAE that Kushner helped manage as an off-the-books foreign policy fund, and that UAE leader Mohamed bin Zayed moved another roughly $1 billion to Israel for Kushner - money a source told Cole was meant for his "personal benefit."

Cole, a former national security reporter at The Intercept who previously produced investigations for ABC and NBC News, says the reporting took him four years. His book is published by Atria/One Signal, a Simon & Schuster imprint.

October is the month of political surprises. If substantiated, this would be a big one. It's also sure to provide endless headlines after midterms, if (when) Democrats take the House. 

Kushner fired back on X. "The allegations made by this author are completely insane, categorically false, and never happened," he wrote. "No bank statements, wire transfer records, account numbers, transaction dates, or other verifiable details were provided to support these extraordinary accusations."

He called the excerpt "a mixture of fantasy, fiction, and advocacy, written by someone who is either deeply disturbed or acting with sinister intent." His lawyer told Cole that "there are no accounts and never were."

.@VanityFair posted an excerpt from a book containing outrageous and categorically false allegations. The allegations made by this author are completely insane and never happened. We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them. No bank statements, wire transfer records, account numbers, transaction dates, or other verifiable details were provided to support these extraordinary accusations. During the period in question, I was one of the most scrutinized people in the world, subjected to intense media coverage, multiple congressional investigations, and a special counsel investigation. I voluntarily cooperated with these investigations, providing over 30 hours of testimony. None of these allegations ever surfaced, because none of these events ever happened. These are outrageous fabrications being presented as investigative journalism. This is not journalism. It is a mixture of fantasy, fiction, and advocacy, written by someone who is either deeply disturbed or acting with sinister intent.

— Jared Kushner (@jaredkushner) October 22, 2026

Watched through his iPhone

Here's the story. The usual grains of salt apply.

Cole's account begins in late 2017, when Dutch military intelligence learned that a Russian GRU operative - a dark web hacker specializing in stolen bank data - was headed to the UK. With British cooperation, the Dutch gave him a choice: work for them or face espionage charges. He flipped.

The Russian gave the Dutch access to a GRU server in Rostov, where they found screenshots of Kushner's iPhone. By early 2018, Dutch hackers had found their own way into the phone. They couldn't turn it into a microphone, but they could see his screen. They watched him log into a UAE bank account that had received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan, Cole writes.

Cole's first tip, in the spring of 2020, went further. A source told him Kushner appeared to have moved significant sums from the account to people including "a warlord, a mercenary and a one-time hit man." Cole writes that he told the source it sounded preposterous. Six months later, a second source confirmed knowing about Kushner and transfers from a UAE account.

The accounts

According to Cole, the arrangement grew out of a bigger offer. Early in Trump's first term, bin Zayed and Saudi Arabia's Mohammed bin Salman discussed putting more than $10 billion into a slush fund to advance the new administration's foreign policy goals - including, Cole writes, helping pay for Trump's border wall to secure a second term. The idea fizzled.

Instead, the two royals put at least $2 billion into at least two accounts for Kushner, whose family company at the time faced a billion-dollar loan coming due on its flagship Manhattan tower, 666 Fifth Avenue.

The first account, which Cole calls "Alpha," was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, chaired by bin Zayed's brother Tahnoon bin Zayed. Starting in 2017, the Saudis and Emiratis allegedly moved roughly $750 million into it through Azerbaijan, where, Cole writes, some banks will swap riyals or dirhams for dollars for a 6 to 7 percent fee, leaving auditors nothing to trace.

The account belonged to the Watani Al Emarat Foundation, a government-funded charity Cole says doubled as a cover for the UAE's secret military and intelligence operations abroad, including weapons purchases. Kushner was allegedly a signatory, with access to a fund he and bin Zayed partly managed as they chased a grand bargain on Israel.

A source who knew of the deal told Cole that Kushner promised bin Zayed he would push the UAE's agenda with Trump if the Emiratis joined the fund. Such slush funds are routine for the Gulf monarchies, the source said: "A billion or two is nothing for them."

Kushner's lawyer denied that he had any knowledge of or connection to the charity, its then-director Dherar Belhoul Al Falasi, or any UAE bank account, and said he complied with all legal requirements in dealing with foreign governments.

By the spring of 2018, Cole writes, bin Zayed had moved roughly another $1 billion to Israel, again via Azerbaijan. A person briefed on the arrangement said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu encouraged Kushner to keep it at Israel's central bank, which handles only government money, where it would look like a government account.

Netanyahu required Kushner to notify him before making any transactions, Cole writes, with messages relayed through then-U.S. Ambassador David Friedman. A person who helped Kushner move money out of Israel told Cole much of it went to accounts in Cyprus.

Friedman denied any knowledge of UAE money for Kushner or passing messages on his behalf. "I know absolutely nothing about any of these allegations," he said, calling the claims about his own role "100% false." Cole acknowledges it is unclear whether the Dutch ever saw this second account.

Cole also describes a third account. As Kushner helped negotiate a secret Israeli commitment to defend the UAE from a major Iranian attack, the Emiratis allegedly sent another transfer to Israel's central bank to cover the cost - a rainy-day defense fund.

As a White House employee with access to classified information, Kushner was required to disclose any account on which he was a signatory or beneficiary. Cole says four senior Trump administration officials - two national security advisers, a White House chief of staff and a CIA director - knew of no presidential authorization for him to access a foreign government's bank account.

A former Mueller prosecutor said that if Kushner promised the royals anything in return - even just a word with his father-in-law - he may have violated federal bribery law and the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Kushner's lawyer said he broke no laws while in the White House, and that every arrangement he made with foreign leaders was agreed to by Trump and in America's interest.

Not the first Gulf windfall

In May 2017, Kushner's sister Nicole Kushner Meyer pitched Chinese investors in Beijing on One Journal Square, a Kushner Companies tower in Jersey City seeking money through the EB-5 program, in which a $500,000 investment buys a path to a green card. She told the room her brother had left the business to join the Trump administration, and the company later apologized.

In February 2018, The Washington Post reported that officials from the UAE, China, Israel and Mexico had privately discussed exploiting Kushner's business dealings and inexperience, with Emirati officials viewing him as particularly manipulable. His security clearance was downgraded around the same time.

Trump ordered chief of staff John Kelly to grant Kushner a top-secret clearance anyway, over the concerns of career intelligence officials and White House counsel Don McGahn, The New York Times reported in 2019 - weeks after Trump told the paper he had not intervened.

In 2017, Kushner Companies reportedly sought a billion-dollar bailout from Qatari officials while Kushner advised Trump to back the Saudi-led blockade of Qatar, according to Senate Finance Democrats. The next year, Brookfield rescued 666 Fifth Avenue with a $1.3 billion, 99-year lease. Qatar's sovereign wealth fund was a major Brookfield backer, though the firm said Qatari representatives had no involvement, and Sen. Ron Wyden and Rep. Joaquin Castro later probed whether the deal shaped Trump's Qatar policy.

Six months after Kushner left the White House, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund put $2 billion into his new firm, Affinity Partners - overruling its own screening panel, which had flagged the "inexperience" of Kushner's team and called its operations "unsatisfactory in all aspects," The New York Times reported. The fund is run by bin Salman.

By 2024, roughly 99% of Affinity's money came from foreign sources, mainly the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, according to Wyden, then the Senate Finance chairman, who said those governments were paying Kushner tens of millions of dollars in fees a year. In September 2025, Affinity joined PIF and Silver Lake in a $55 billion deal to take Electronic Arts private.

Kushner is now back inside the administration as Trump's special envoy. In March, Wyden - who had already referred Kushner to the Justice Department over possible foreign-agent violations - and House Oversight's top Democrat, Robert Garcia, demanded answers about Kushner soliciting billions from Gulf sovereign wealth funds while co-leading U.S. Middle East negotiations. Wyden said Kushner is "on the payroll of the Saudi government."

items.title: California Officials Blame 'Vendor Error' For Sending Thousands Of Duplicate Ballots
items.content_text:
California Officials Blame 'Vendor Error' For Sending Thousands Of Duplicate Ballots

Authored by Luis Cornelio via Headline USA,

A California county sent duplicate mail-in ballots to thousands of voters in what officials have characterized as a printing error, raising questions about election security amid heightened federal scrunity.

items.title: Florida Mayor Charged With Grand Theft From COVID Relief Program She Helped Create
items.content_text:
Florida Mayor Charged With Grand Theft From COVID Relief Program She Helped Create

Authored by Jill McLaughlin via The Epoch Times,

State authorities arrested the mayor of the central Florida city of Kissimmee on Oct. 21, charging her with grand theft and organized fraud over funds she received from a COVID-19 relief program.

Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa maintains her innocence after state charges were filed Oct. 21, 2026, accusing her of grant theft and organized fraud. Osceola County Jail

State Attorney General James Uthmeier accused Mayor Jackie Espinosa of illegally granting herself, her husband, and family members $50,000 from a city program she created that was meant to boost small businesses recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic.

Espinosa created, funded, expanded, and promoted the Kissimmee Business Boost 2.0 for small businesses and submitted her applications before anyone else on the first day it opened, which prosecutors alleged violated state law.

"The evidence makes very clear there was intent to engage in this conflict of interest, then ultimately abused her office to enrich herself," Uthmeier said during a press conference Wednesday.

The mayor and her family own several local businesses, including the Adanse, Real Estate Gallery, Matador Tacos and Tapas, and Empresas Espinosa. At the time of the applications, they also owned Kissimmee Diner.

Espinosa was handcuffed outside her home and taken to the Osceola County Jail, where she remained on Wednesday afternoon, according to jail records.

She is charged with one count of grand theft and one count of defrauding to obtain property, first- and second-degree felonies, according to Uthmeier.

Espinosa maintains her innocence, her lawyer Migdalia Perez told The Epoch Times.

"This case involves a publicly approved grant program administered by city staff, not a secret scheme to steal taxpayer money," Perez said in an emailed statement.

"The prosecution must establish that the mayor acted with criminal intent. We firmly maintain that she did not.

"There is a fundamental difference between an alleged ethics violation and a criminal offense," Perez added. "The state cannot transform one into the other without proving every element of a crime beyond a reasonable doubt."

Espinosa, who was elected as mayor in 2024, plans to challenge the allegations in court, her attorney said.

A state financial audit of the city's pandemic funding was performed as a routine matter, according to Florida's Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia, who oversees the state's financial services.

Auditors noticed irregularities in the city's Boost program, Ingoglia said, with funds allegedly linked directly and indirectly to the mayor.

"This led my team to look further," Ingoglia said.

During the investigation, auditors say they were allegedly told that some people in the city office attempted to ask Espinosa if her applications represented a conflict of interest, but they didn't get a response, Ingoglia said.

The city manager also allegedly notified her in a text message that the city attorney believed she was prohibited from receiving the grant funds, according to the arrest record.

Espinosa allegedly told the city manager she received the city attorney's opinion but "felt it was confusing," the court document stated.

Florida state law does not allow defendants to avoid criminal liability by claiming to not know they were violating the law, according to prosecutors.

The audit found three applications signed by Espinosa and filed before all other applications the day the funds became available, according to Ingoglia.

A couple walks in front of a house in Kissimmee, Fla., on Jan. 11, 2023. Marco Bello/Reuters

Of those, one company, Adanse LLC, which Espinosa legally retains 100 percent ownership of, received $20,000 in relief funds.

Her husband's company received $15,000 in funds, the audit found.

Ingolia said he and his team were with law enforcement when they arrested the mayor at her home in Tallahassee on Wednesday morning.

"I am proud of the outstanding work that my auditing team and Criminal Investigations Division did to uncover the alleged misuse of taxpayer dollars and to ensure that Jackie Espinosa's corruption did not go without recourse," Ingoglia said in a social media post.

A state ethics probe found Espinosa violated three ethics rules in July, which prompted the city commission to hold an impeachment vote against her.

The vote stalled after the commission deadlocked last month.

City commissioners also hired a special prosecutor to oversee the ethics complaint.

Espinosa faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted on all charges. A bond amount had not been set.

The city of Kissimmee said there had been no effects on its operations from the mayor's ordeal and regular business has continued.

"The city is prepared to follow the process outlined in the City Charter if a suspension occurs," Spokesperson Alibeth Suarez told The Epoch Times in an email.

"There are no impacts to city operations, which continue under the leadership of the City Manager and within the City's Council-Manager form of government."

items.title: UN Says 8,513 Casualties In Yemen Since August, Over 250K Displaced
items.content_text:
UN Says 8,513 Casualties In Yemen Since August, Over 250K Displaced

There are new, grim numbers out of Yemen, after fierce fighting has been raging for many weeks going back to late August renewed war between the Saudi coalition (and its government in Aden), and the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The UN's World Health Organization on Thursday announced its tally of at least 8,513 casualties in the Yemen conflict since August. This is as of Oct.19, the WHO indicated.

According to the breakdown, this included 1,574 fatalities, and 6,939 others injured and wounded. The organization did not specify whether these were civilians or military personnel.

The WHO indicated further that over just the last eight-day period (counting backward from Oct.19), 292 people were killed and 1,048 others were injured.

Civilians have certainly borne a huge brunt of the renewed conflict, also with attacks spilling over into Saudi territory - where over 20 civilians have died, and cities and airports and energy sites have been targeted.

Al Jazeera reported earlier this week that at least a quarter-million people in Yemen have been displaced, which includes populations on both sides of the fighting.

"More than 250,000 people have been internally displaced in Yemen since the country’s war reignited in July, the United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) has said, as fighting between Houthi rebels and forces loyal to the internationally recognized government rages across several fronts," the report said.

"The city of Taiz in southwestern Yemen is at the center of the displacement crisis, accounting for 76 percent of departures and hosting 52 percent of those newly displaced, UNHCR said in a statement on Tuesday," it added.

Additionally, according to the United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR), "about 33,700 families still require shelter assistance amid severe underfunding of the humanitarian response to the war."

Nearly 260,000 Displaced by Fighting in #Yemen Since August, UN Says Nearly 260,000 people have fled their homes in Yemen since fighting escalated in August, with almost half seeking refuge in #Taiz Governorate, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said. The UN Human Rights Office has verified 57 civilian deaths and 194 injuries. Children accounted for half of those killed. Humanitarian partners have provided food, hygiene kits and emergency cash to more than 174,000 displaced people despite difficult operating conditions. Newly displaced families cited shelter as their most urgent need, followed by food and cash assistance. OCHA called on all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, uphold international humanitarian law and allow the safe and sustained passage of aid and essential commercial goods into and across Taiz.

— Yemen Newsroom (@yemen_newsroom) October 22, 2026

The region has experienced on-and-off outbreaks of war and fighting going all the way back to 2014, when the Saudi-backed government began losing ground to the popular Houthi rebels. At one point the US was much more directly assisting the Saudi air campaign, but currently is said to only be playing an intelligence and advisory role.

Saudi coalition airstrikes have also gone back years, and the new outbreak of fighting has seen hundreds of air raids, which are especially devastating for civilians particularly in urban centers. The Houthis have in turn pummeled Saudi coalition areas with missiles and drones, which have also more frequently been sent across the border into the kingdom itself.

items.title: "Not To My Knowledge": Ilhan Omar Can't Quite Rule Out Marrying Her Brother In Wild Interview... And Trump Noticed

"Not To My Knowledge": Ilhan Omar Can't Quite Rule Out Marrying Her Brother In Wild Interview... And Trump Noticed

As the investigation into whether Ilhan Omar married her brother to scam US immigration, the Minnesota Democrat just stepped in it, big time. 

In her first interview since Homeland Security Investigations agents searched her Washington home last week, the Minnesota Democrat sat down with MS NOW's Chris Hayes, about as friendly a venue as exists on cable. She called the decade-old claim that her ex-husband Ahmed Nur Said Elmi is her brother "insane." Then Hayes gave her the layup, asking whether there was some "weird kernel of truth" to it. Her answer was "Not to my knowledge."

Regular readers will recall that earlier this week we flagged a report that federal investigators are using DNA to probe the "married her brother" claim. So the timing could have been better. The clip went everywhere within the hour:

YIKES: Ilhan Omar was just asked if she married her brother on Live TV

Her answer: "Not to my knowledge..."

WHAT?!

She can't even say "NO"?!

What other person would answer this question like that?

Things are about to get bad for Ilhan. pic.twitter.com/n8wwJb4puy

— Benny Johnson (@bennyjohnson) October 22, 2026

In other words, the one question her own side's friendliest interviewer was guaranteed to ask is the one she didn't answer with a "no." Below we walk through what she actually said, how fast the White House pounced, and why "not to my knowledge" is a strange hill to stand on with a federal grand jury in the background.

"Which Is Insane"

Omar claims the allegation started on a Somali blog and was picked up by "right-wing conspiracy theorists in Minneapolis":

"...they just kind of went and found random people who were like, 'She introduced us. She introduced him to us and said he was her brother.' Which is insane."

HAYES: "He was not - you were not related to him at all? Not that there's not some weird kernel of truth that through some-"

OMAR: "Not to my knowledge."

The generous reading is that Hayes's question was oddly phrased (a "kernel of truth" through "some" mechanism) and Omar was hedging against a hypothetical rather than admitting anything. The less generous reading is that when the stakes are denaturalization, people tend to choose their words very carefully. Make of that what you will.

"That's An Answer A Lot Of Us Assume"

It took the president about an hour and a half. After his South Carolina rally, Trump was asked about the clip, according to Townhall:

🚨 LMFAO! President Trump just FLAMED Ilhan Omar for answering "NOT TO MY KNOWLEDGE" when asked if she married her brother

"Yeah, well 'not to my knowledge'... that's NOT a good answer. That's an answer a LOT of us assume." 🤣

She's TOTALLY cooked! 😂 https://t.co/Mljre01LVM pic.twitter.com/GpHvia7rh2

— Nick Sortor (@nicksortor) October 22, 2026

That's an answer that a lot of us assume." The rest of the online right was less restrained, and we will spare readers most of it.

Omar's brother hasn't made it easy on her. In a 2012 Instagram post after Ilhan's daughter was born, her brother/husband posted "Nieces, fresh out of the vagina!" 

About That Raid

The brother line overshadowed the rest of a fairly revealing interview. According to the New York Post, Omar said:

  • Agents "went room by room" and "took 17 items," including cellphones, her daughter's old phone, her husband's notebooks, a Somali phrase book and a camera.
  • She disputed reports that investigators got her DNA in the search: "I would have seen if they did take anything that had contained DNA."
  • She called the search "intrusive but polite," adding that agents "even folded some of my clothing that were not folded." Service with a smile.
  • Asked about the financial disclosure that once put her household's net worth at about $30 million (later revised), she described herself as "working class" and living "paycheck to paycheck," with a 2016 Toyota Camry and two rented homes.

She also said the people who searched her home "literally have" her late father's naturalization papers, which is the crux of the case, since she says she became a citizen at 17 through him. That line got its own viral moment:

Ilhan Omar on her father's naturalization papers: "The people who knocked on my door searching for papers literally have his papers"

DHS: The records do not exist. pic.twitter.com/zHQ9koHnrI

— Benny Johnson (@bennyjohnson) October 22, 2026

What The Feds Are Actually Probing

Per the Post, the immigration case is run out of the Minnesota US Attorney's Office and may involve possible false statements about her birth date on immigration documents. A separate probe into her and her husband's finances is being run out of the DC US Attorney's Office. The Wall Street Journal reported more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, including to relatives. A source told the Post that if her citizenship was obtained through concealment or misrepresentation, by her or by her father, the administration will seek to denaturalize and deport her. Omar denies any wrongdoing: "I'm confident in my truth."

Put differently, the "brother" question isn't just tabloid fodder: if the 2009 marriage was a sham for immigration purposes, it goes to the heart of a fraud case, which is why "no" would have been the obvious answer to give.

items.title: October Election Surprise Season Is Here!
items.content_text:
October Election Surprise Season Is Here!

Authored by Ed Dowd: Beyond the Narrative via Substack,

October Surprise Season is back, right on schedule. The phenomenon is simple and well documented. Basically in the final weeks before a high-stakes election, an event, leak, crisis, or carefully timed disclosure appears that is meant to shift momentum, freeze the narrative, or force voters to reassess. The classic modern example remains 1980, when the Iran hostage crisis and the fear of a last minute Carter breakthrough gave the phrase its name. Bill Casey, running Reagan's campaign, used the term explicitly.

Decades later the pattern repeats with variations:

  • · George W. Bush's 1976 DUI surfacing days before the 2000 election

  • · The Trump Access Hollywood tape and the late Clinton email revelations in 2016

  • · Hurricane Sandy in October 2012 and Obama's response was positive for his campaign

  • · Assorted foreign policy or scandal drops that dominate cable and social media for 72 hours

The common thread is timing. With early voting, mail-in ballots, and compressed news cycles, an October event has maximum leverage and minimal time for full scrutiny or counter narratives. Whether organic or engineered, the incentives favor dramatic movement right before ballots are finalized.

Informal X Poll

On Tuesday October 20th I asked my X followers a direct question: two weeks until the midterms, so what will be the October surprise? The replies clustered around a few themes. One high-engagement response noted that USAID had been gutted and therefore "no money for surprises this year." I found that response quite humorous.

Another leaned toward nothing at all, arguing that the institutional interests prefer a blue team outcome so certain legislation (amnesty, digital ID, conscription) can pass with Trump's signature and the political blame can be shared...essentially a uniparty viewpoint.

A third predicted an Iran war escalation paired with a stock-market crash. Cyberattack scenarios, grid disruptions, and stock market rug-pulls also appeared repeatedly.

A forth expressed the feeling among many that you could post almost any absurd answer and it would seem plausible...a sign of the times.

The distribution was telling as relatively few expected a classic personal scandal or policy announcement that would clearly favor one side. More people expected either controlled chaos or deliberate inaction designed to produce a specific legislative or institutional result.

Well Timed NSA Cyber Security Alert

Yesterday the NSA issued a rare public cyber security alert. Organizations running PHP, the language powering an estimated 70 percent of websites, were told to prepare for updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities or take systems offline until mitigated. The flaws, reportedly identified with the assistance of frontier AI models from OpenAI's Patch the Planet effort and independently by Wiz, can provide a direct path to a server's file system or database. OpenAI described the issue as one of the most impactful in recent memory; patches were released the same day, and multiple governments echoed the urgency. The alert itself is legitimate on its face as PHP is foundational infrastructure. The timing is what stands out. Midterms are thirteen days away. Election administration, poll-book systems, voter-registration portals, and related state and local web applications are not immune to the same underlying technology stack. If unpatched or poorly patched systems are present in any voting-related infrastructure, the window for exploitation is now open. Even if the immediate risk is limited, the episode supplies a ready-made explanation for later anomalies: "cyber incident," "system offline for security," "delayed tabulation." History shows that once such an explanation exists, institutional actors have strong incentives to use it.

Potential Positive Trump Administration Surprises

Positive surprises for the incumbent side are also possible and would follow the same October logic. A credible framework that ends or freezes the Ukraine conflict, or a de-escalation agreement with Iran that reopens the Strait of Hormuz and stabilizes energy prices, would be classic late election cycle good news. Both theaters have already produced significant market and political volatility. A sudden diplomatic breakthrough that can be framed as "peace through strength" would dominate coverage, potentially shift polling among independents, and complicate Democratic messaging on foreign policy and inflation. Whether such deals materialize depends on counterparties who do not answer to U.S. election calendars, but the political incentive to announce progress is obvious and well understood by every administration.

Bottom Line: Post-Election Day Questions May Be The Surprise

The more durable issue, however, sits after Election Day. Mail-in and early voting volumes remain elevated in key jurisdictions. Statistical anomalies in the timing and distribution of ballots have been documented in prior cycles and have not been fully resolved to the satisfaction of large segments of the electorate. Chain-of-custody gaps, observer access limitations, and the continued use of systems whose source code and operational procedures are not fully transparent create legitimate questions about final tallies. I personally believe the system is broken and not secure from fraud. A cyber alert thirteen days out does not resolve those questions rather it potentially expands the set of post-election explanations available to whichever side loses. In that environment, the legitimacy of the reported results and the willingness of institutions and the public to accept them will matter more than whatever headline arrives between now and November 3. The October surprise, if it comes, will be noisy. The quieter and more consequential question is whether the post-election count can be shown, with evidence, to reflect the actual votes cast. That standard has not been consistently met in recent cycles, and the current technical and procedural environment does not make it more likely. Post election mayhem is my personal odds-on favorite.

"There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens." Ecclesiastes 3:1

items.title: Still 'A Very High Mountain Ahead' To Achieve Ukraine Peace: Vance
items.content_text:
Still 'A Very High Mountain Ahead' To Achieve Ukraine Peace: Vance

It has been a long, long time since this much optimism has persisted when it comes to the chances of achieving a Russia-Ukraine peace deal.

There are reports that trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the US will finally soon happen in the wake of Steve Witkoff's meeting with President Putin this week. A high level meeting is reportedly being scheduled for as early as next month; however, some top White House officials are also injecting some key caveats and realism.

Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that Russia and Ukraine are still too far apart to reach a peace agreement, despite at least tentatively seeing eye to eye on resuming US-backed negotiations.

In a fresh interview with Forbes, Vance said."I think both countries have agreed to come to the negotiating table. The reason we have not yet reached a peace agreement is that they are simply too far apart on the details of those negotiations."

He praised Witkoff for his efforts at getting the warring sides back to the negotiating bale: "He is optimistic. The nature of these things is that you make an attempt, see how far you can get, and then come back to it again. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't," the Vice President continued.

Vance further stated:

"We are trying to do difficult things, knowing we have a very high mountain ahead of us. We are trying anyway."

Putin aide Yuri Ushakov announced in the middle of this week that Moscow has agreed to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the United States in November.

President Putin has meanwhile not changed his tune, emphasizing in fresh media remarks that the goals of the 'special military operation' will be achieved with or without a deal...

Putin on Ukraine: I think that we can reach an agreement. We agree with that. But if someone wants otherwise, fine, it will be otherwise. But in any case, we will accomplish our tasks, and all the goals of the "special military operation" will be achieved. https://t.co/qjXsjocMNf

— Clash Report (@clashreport) October 22, 2026

The Kremlin on Wednesday still hailed that there have been significant changes in Washington's posture in Ukraine, with Ushakov having noted that these changes caused Moscow's stance to in turn be "re-evaluated, taking into account the signals received from the Americans."

Are Radicals Training In Paris?

Authored by Silvio Canto, Jr. via American Thinker,

Guess who is traveling to Paris for a training seminar on how to commit terrorist acts and destroy historic sites?

I'm sure that the first class is about destroying all of those statues of Lincoln and Jefferson.

Let's check this report from Kamal Sultan in the NY Post:

A Minnesota rapper who traveled to France to join escalating riots has urged white people to "raise hell" and "f–k s–t up" as part of a revolution on American soil, The Post discovered. And communist-linked groups in the US may be working to bring that hell to the nation's capital.

Artist Tufawon, whose real name is Rafael Gonzalez Jr., joined Swedish activist Greta Thunberg outside Paul Éluard, the high school at the heart of the leftist protests marred by violence, looting and arson.

He addressed balaclava-clad protesters before performing his song "No One Is Illegal," and riling up the crowd with chants of "f–k ICE" and "ICE out."

"All power to the people," the 40-year-old from Minneapolis boasted to his fans on Facebook. "After returning home from France I can clearly see how we need to become far more radicalized in the states.

"We have to be more enraged. Our comfort is hindering our progress. It really and truly needs to be white people that go outside and raise hell if we want to see revolution.

We want to see revolution?

items.title: Major US Banks Are Detecting Unauthorized AI Agents Accessing Customer Accounts
items.content_text:
Major US Banks Are Detecting Unauthorized AI Agents Accessing Customer Accounts

America’s largest banks are scrambling to defend themselves against a new and rapidly evolving security threat: artificial intelligence agents gaining access to customer accounts, sometimes behaving in ways that appear to go beyond what their human users originally authorized, according to Axios. 

Major financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo and Citigroup are confronting the growing presence of third-party AI assistants inside their banking platforms. Some institutions have detected unauthorized agent activity, while others are concerned about cases in which AI systems appear to initiate actions without explicit instructions from account holders.

The problem is becoming particularly difficult because banks cannot always distinguish between a legitimate customer accessing an account, an AI assistant acting with that customer's permission, and a potentially rogue agent operating outside its intended authority.

In many cases, customers themselves are providing AI tools with their banking credentials so the software can perform financial tasks on their behalf. While those arrangements may be voluntary, they frequently violate bank policies requiring account holders to maintain control of their login information.

More troubling is what happens once an AI agent gains access. Depending on the permissions it has been given, an assistant could potentially initiate purchases, transfer money or perform other financial transactions. Bank executives are increasingly concerned about the possibility of these systems making consequential decisions without adequate human oversight.

The Axios report out Thursday morning reported instances of agents interacting with bank call centers, as well as activity suggesting that certain systems may have attempted to act independently of their users' instructions. The developments have prompted several Wall Street institutions to begin tightening access to their platforms.

Morgan Stanley has reportedly started blocking third-party AI agents, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citigroup have also moved to restrict their activities. A Chase spokesperson cautioned customers against sharing account usernames and passwords, while Morgan Stanley said it had not identified instances of rogue AI agents accessing its systems.

The industry is not necessarily opposed to AI-powered financial assistants altogether. In fact, many banks already permit limited, read-only access to customer information through authorized third-party applications, including budgeting and personal finance software.

That model could provide a compromise for AI agents, allowing them to analyze balances, review transactions and help customers manage their finances without granting them the authority to actually move money.

But even that distinction is becoming more complicated as AI systems grow increasingly autonomous.

Banking executives acknowledge that consumers will likely demand more sophisticated AI assistants capable of handling financial tasks in the future. The challenge is developing safeguards that allow those capabilities without exposing customers to unauthorized transactions, compromised accounts or unpredictable automated behavior.

Compounding the problem is the speed at which the technology is evolving. Even banks with enormous cybersecurity budgets and extensive experience protecting critical financial infrastructure are struggling to keep pace with new vulnerabilities.

Financial institutions are consequently investing not only in preventing unauthorized AI activity, but also in preparing for potential failures. According to Axios, some are developing contingency plans for rapidly securing accounts and restoring customer access following a serious AI-related security incident.

The broader concern is that AI agents are advancing faster than the systems designed to supervise them. And in an industry where a single unauthorized action can have immediate financial consequences, the distinction between an assistant following instructions and an autonomous system acting on its own is becoming an increasingly important security problem.

For Wall Street, the challenge is no longer simply figuring out how to incorporate artificial intelligence into banking. It's figuring out how to keep increasingly capable AI systems from doing things that neither the banks nor their customers intended.

items.title: 浏览器 Arc 将于 12 月关闭
items.content_text: The Browser Company 宣布其浏览器 Arc 将于 12 月 22 日关闭，用户将无法再能启动应用。Arc 基于 Chromium，于 2023 年释出了 1.0 版本，但 2024 年就停止了开发，2025 年 5 月宣布它正在开发 AI 驱动的浏览器 Dia。Arc 从 10 月 22 日起无法创建新的 Arc 账号，11 月 23 日起停用部分功能，12 月 22 日无法启动应用，Arc 账户将被停用，个人数据会在 30 天内被删除。The Browser Company 表示 Arc 用户可通过数据导出功能无缝使用其全力开发的新浏览器 Dia，声称用户在 Arc 中使用的浏览器功能在 Dia 中均可免费使用，而 AI 功能则是可选使用的。

items.title: Switch 2 越狱能运行自制程序
items.content_text: 研究员 Sammy Hajhamid 利用软件漏洞在 Switch 2 上实现越狱，而且能运行自制程序。越狱利用了一个专门运行在任天堂硬件上的编程环境和解释器 SmileBasic 4。Hajhamid 使用 OpenAI 的 Codex 对 SmileBasic 的语言解释器进行探测，花了两周时间发现了一个 32 位整数溢出漏洞，利用该漏洞能对部分系统内存进行读写操作。他在此基础上从 Switch 2 内部找到了其它漏洞，提权获得任意读写权限。他之后演示了在越狱的游戏机上运行自制程序。SmileBasic 4 已从任天堂的 Switch eShop 中下架，漏洞可能会在后续的固件更新中修复。

items.title: KeePassXC 2.8.0 释出
items.content_text: 开源密码管理器项目 KeePassXC 释出了 v2.8.0。KeePassXC 代表 KeePass Cross-Platform Community Edition，是 KeePassX 的一个分支，而 KeePassX 则是基于 Qt 构建的 KeePass 克隆版本，但已停止维护。KeePassXC 2.8.0 带来了用户期待的新功能，大量 bug 修复和安全修正。主要特性包括：Qt 的版本从 Qt5 升级到 Qt6，Wayland(Linux) 下支持 Auto-Type，可自定义快捷键，使用外部工具实现远程数据库同步，macOS 支持密码快速解锁，Linux 下支持通过 Polkit 快速解锁，Windows 下提供了支持 ARM64 架构的原生版本，等等。

items.title: eMudhra 退出全球 CA 业务
items.content_text: 在曝出惊人丑闻之后，印度公司 eMudhra  宣布退出全球 CA 业务，将专注于核心企业解决方案和信任服务而非 SSL/TLS 相关业务。它是印度唯一一个被主流浏览器信任的 Root CA 机构。截至 2026 年，公司已发行逾 6000 万张证书。此前 eMudhra 的八个中间证书的私钥泄漏，而这些私钥被发现是极其简单的数字如 4。该公司在声明中称这些简单密钥是“多重人为错误”导致的。相关密钥是在 2025 年  4 月 30 日生成，它使用专门的硬件安全模块生成了一组密钥，但软件脚本的一个缺陷导致其生成了另一组较弱的密钥，由于两组密钥名称相似，结果其员工选择了弱密钥组。

items.title: 趋势科技在公开的内核邮件列表上披露内核漏洞
items.content_text: 趋势科技的安全团队 Zero Day Initiative 向人人可访问的内核邮件列表上递交了一系列新发现的内核漏洞。按照惯例，漏洞应该递交到不对外公开的安全邮件列表。递交的部分漏洞没有补丁，部分漏洞已有补丁在测试，这些漏洞的 CVSS 风险评分最高为 9.0。稳定版内核维护者 Greg Kroah-Hartman 批评安全研究人员将漏洞报告递交到公共的邮件列表。而在 AI 辅助漏洞发现时代，此类的漏洞报告越来越多。

items.title: 科学家揭示低温延缓衰老的机制
items.content_text: 适度低温已被证明能有效延长动物寿命，延缓与衰老相关的机能衰退。但低温延缓衰老的分子机制是什么？研究人员利用秀丽隐杆线虫（Caenorhabditis elegans ）发现，低温会触发代谢物 dihydrobiopterin (BH2)的大量产生，其中肌肉充当了中央工厂的作用，负责合成 BH2，BH2 随后输送至身体其它组织，诱导氨基酸酪氨酸（tyrosine）的合成，它有助于维持蛋白质稳态，在衰老过程中促进组织健康。论文发表在《自然》期刊上。研究还发现，同时补充 BH2 和酪氨酸能在秀丽隐杆线虫及细胞培养物上再现低温的部分有益效应，即便在标准温度或更高温度下也能显著延长寿命。研究人员强调，就目前研究而言，开发出一种能重现低温长寿效应的药丸还为时过早。

items.title: 逾半数美国人认为 AI 对社会有害
items.content_text: 根据 ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos 的调查，57%的美国人认为 AI 对社会有害，42%的人认为它对社会有益。仅有 2% 的人认为它对社会极其有益，17% 的人认为它对社会极其有害。与年长者相比，年轻的美国人更有可能认为 AI 对社会有害：在 30 岁以下的美国人中，65% 的人持此观点；在 30-39 岁的群体中，这一比例为 59%。而在 40 岁及以上的美国人中，认为 AI 对社会有害的比例相对较低，但也超过半数（53%）。在民主党人（63%）和独立人士（58%）中，多数人认为 AI 对社会有害；共和党人认为有益有害的比例差不多，51% 的人认为  AI 对社会有益，47% 的人认为它对社会有害。当谈及 AI 对个人自身的影响时，50% 的人认为 AI 对自己有益，49% 的人认为对自己有害。持负面态度的人群立场更为强烈——认为 AI 对自己极其有害的人数（15%）是认为其极其有益人数（3%）的五倍。多数共和党人（57%）认为 AI 对自己个人有益，而多数民主党人（55%）则认为 AI 对自己个人有害。无党派人士对于 AI 对自己个人而言究竟是好（50%）还是坏（49%）比例差不多。

items.title: 研究识别出第一位企业心理病态者
items.content_text: 一项新研究指出，有毒企业领导人身上所见的性格特征可追溯到一位 400 年前的荷兰东印度公司的企业官员。该公司的商户部经理 Jeronimus Cornelisz 可能是最早有文献记录的企业心理病态者。研究发现，他表现出了与企业心理病态者相关的全部 10 项核心特征。这些特征包括：利用个人魅力博取信任；在身边聚集忠诚的追随者；清除潜在的挑战者；在竞争对手之间制造分裂；营造恐惧氛围；出问题时推卸责任；将追求权力、金钱和控制权置于一切之上。荷兰东印度公司是世界上第一家跨国股份制企业；1602 年该公司在阿姆斯特丹开设了世界最早的证券交易所之一。研究认为，Cornelisz 的案例表明，早在资本主义萌芽时期，受权力、财富和个人晋升欲望驱动的人，就已被商业性企业所吸引。研究聚焦于 1629 年发生在西澳大利亚海岸外岛屿上的 Batavia 沉船惨案。沉船事故后，约 200 名幸存者被困在几座孤岛上。由于高管已乘船前往今天的雅加达寻求救援，身为经理的 Cornelisz 便成了幸存者中职位最高的企业代表。在他的领导下，约有 100 名男女老少遭到杀害，部分女性还遭受了性暴力。Cornelisz 将这些杀戮辩解为节省食物和水资源的一种手段，而这些谋杀同时也铲除了他眼中的竞争对手。

items.title: 毅力号行使距离超机遇号刷新历史记录
items.content_text: 毅力号火星车创下新的世界纪录——它在地外天体表面的行驶里程，超过了此前所有探测器。10月11日，它的里程表读数达到28.10英里（45.22公里），超越了此前由机遇号保持的28.06英里（45.16公里）纪录。机遇号于2004至2018年间在火星开展探测。机遇号耗费近15年才跑完该里程，而毅力号仅用时5年半。这一里程碑事件发生在它的第2006个火星日。毅力号能长途行进，一大核心原因是搭载了先进的自主行驶系统。这套系统名为 AutoNav。依靠它火星车大多时候不需要等待地球发来详细行驶指令，就能自主在火星地表认路。行进过程中，毅力号持续拍摄周边影像，绘制包含障碍物信息的三维地图，在地面操控人员选定的目的地之间自行规划安全路线。该系统可以让火星车以接近最高速度行驶，单个火星日最多可前进1351英尺（412米）。毅力号超过90%的行驶里程都依靠AutoNav自主评估地形。与之对比，机遇号及其孪生探测器勇气号早期自主导航系统，仅能自主评估约5%的行驶路段。

items.title: 因加州考虑征收亿万富翁税扎克伯格有意离开
items.content_text: Meta 周三警告，如果加州通过亿万富翁税，公司 CEO 扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）可能会离开加州迁往他处。扎克伯格已向公司特别委员会告知了这一可能性。据 Meta 在监管文件中披露的计划，为了让扎克伯格未来八年继续留在加州领导公司，公司将设立一类新股票，允许他出售在 Meta 中最多一半的经济权益，同时保留投票控制权。亿万富翁税提案已列入加州 11 月的选票，提议对亿万富翁的资产一次性征收 5% 的税款。Google 联合创始人Sergey Brin 已投入超过 1 亿美元反对该提案。英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋则是少数表示不介意缴纳税款的加州亿万富翁。

items.title: OpenClaw 作者称他上个月花掉了千万美元的 Tokens
items.content_text: 周三旧金山举行的 Cloudflare Connect 2026 大会上，OpenAI 技术部成员、OpenClaw 作者 Peter Steinberger 在与 Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht 对话时透露，上个月运行 AI 工作负载消耗了价值约 1000 万美元的 Token。当然这笔支出不用他自己掏钱，他花的是投资人的钱。Steinberger 称自己拥有几乎无限的 Token 预算。Steinberger 认为，未来每个人都会拥有某种智能体——它们能持续运行、进行思考，在全天候为你提供帮助，甚至能预判你未来可能需要什么，这样你或许无需提问就能直接获得答案。

items.title: 美光桃园厂员工罢工一天
items.content_text: 美光在台有两座工厂，其中桃园厂工会与资方就员工利润分红未能达成共识，星期四（10月22日）发动24小时罢工；台中厂工会于周三签署劳资协议，但未公布具体内容。桃园厂工会星期四上午9时起，在厂区门口展开为期24小时的罢工行动，预计持续至星期五（23日）上午9时。美光桃园厂约有3000名员工，其中约2400人为工会会员；台中厂则有约1万2300名员工，工会会员约1万1000人。桃园厂工会的主要诉求是，要求建立以公司营业利润15%为基础的长期员工分红制度，并将奖金发放方式由每年改为每季，以改善过往绩效奖金（IPP）不透明、分配不对称的问题。

items.title: EA 关闭 BioWare 工作室，取消《质量效应》新作开发
items.content_text: EA 裁员约 400 人，关闭 BioWare 工作室，取消《质量效应》新作开发。BioWare 工作室成立于 1995 年，创始人是医生，2007 年出售给 EA，创始人在 2012 年左右退出。该工作室的游戏包括了《博德之门》、《无冬之夜》、《星战旧共和国武士》、《翡翠帝国》、《龙腾世纪》和《质量效应》系列，以及《圣歌》。其中旨在获得持续收入的服务型游戏《圣歌》饱受批评，游戏于 2021 年停止开发，服务器于 2026 年 1 月关闭。BioWare 的最后一款游戏是 2024 年发布的 《龙腾世纪：影障守护者》，该作品的销量未达预期，工作室在 2025 年大规模裁员，只剩下约 50 人从事《质量效应》新作的早期开发。BioWare 在官网发表了一封告别信，简要回顾了工作室的历史。前 BioWare 员工之后泄漏了《质量效应》新作《宇宙》的预告片。

items.title: 坏苹果效应：人们会效仿他人的违规行为
items.content_text: 俗话说，一颗烂苹果，能毁掉一整桶好苹果。发表在《Proceedings of the Royal Society B》期刊上的一项研究再次为坏苹果效应提供了证据。这项研究旨在探讨个人如何在社会情境中做出是否违规的决策。研究人员说，很多人可能以为自己的决策是完全自主做出的，但事实上在很多情况下，我们的行为深受他人的影响。研究人员在美国招募了 750 名参与者进行了一项在线实验，共和党人和民主党人的比例大致相当。研究结果显示了他人的选择如何产生影响：看到别人遵守规则会略微降低个人违规，看到别人略微违规则会略微增加自己的违规，看到他人明显违规则会明显增加自己的违规。而当违规者与自己属于同一阵营，坏苹果效应则会更显著，表明政治立场一致的人更容易相互影响。研究期间有三分之一的参与者始终遵守规则，尽管这么做并不能获得最大收益。

items.title: 鸟类是地球最重要的养分搬运者之一
items.content_text: 鸟类在塑造地球化学环境上的作用被低估了，它们是地球最重要的养分搬运者之一。研究人员揭示了鸟类如何通过自身的排泄物和身躯，将养分在陆地、湖泊和海洋之间搬运。这一过程深深影响着从土壤和水体的化学性质，到动植物的生长。飞行能力让鸟类能跨越广阔的距离，甚至逾越海洋和山脉等天然屏障。鸟类在处理和循环养分上也极其高效。鸟类的食物摄入率比体型相当的哺乳动物高出约 30%。因此鸟类始终处于进食状态——它们大量摄取富含氮和磷的种子、昆虫、无脊椎动物及果实——并以极高的速率释放出养分。鸟类会将高浓度的养分集中在小片区域内，为当地的植物及其它生物提供关键资源。研究团队发现，饮食的季节性变化会导致鸟类的排泄物成分发生显著改变。春季鸟类摄入较多昆虫，其排泄物氮含量更高；秋季鸟类摄入较多果实和种子，其排泄物碳含量相对更高。根据《State of the World’s Birds》报告，全球 45% 的候鸟物种数量正在下降，可能会导致许多生态系统的肥力下降，进而降低其生产力。

items.content_text: 微软此前披露它的下一代 Xbox 游戏机代号为 Project Helix。根据财富杂志对 Xbox 业务 CEO Asha Sharma 的深度报道：微软计划 2027 年底推出新一代掌机，2028 年底/假期发布新主机，而该主机的售价在 1200-1800 美元之间。由于 AI 热导致内存价格飙升，很多硬件产品都提高了定价，Steam Machine 售价超过 1000 美元，两年前的游戏机 PlayStation 5 Pro 售价达到 900 美元，6 年前的 Xbox Series X 起售价 750 美元。如果微软愿意补贴，售价可能会略微降低。

items.title: AI 增加了英国公务员的工作量
items.content_text: 自 ChatGPT 问世以来，世界各地的政府部门正经历针对监管机构与官方单位的投诉、请求和回应数量的异常暴增。法院系统的情况同样如此。以英国为例，英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士的劳动仲裁案件一年内激增了 39%，部分原因在于原告利用 AI 起草诉状；与此同时，面对大批因请不起律师而使用 ChatGPT 拼凑案情的当事人，基层法官和高级法官感到焦头烂额，因为这些案由往往漏洞百出、毫无逻辑。而所有这些繁杂的内容，都需要人工耐心梳理与甄别——毕竟即便被告引用了根本不存在的判例，也不意味着其背后就没有合理的冤屈。英国政府特别顾问抱怨称，各大部门正淹没在由 AI 生成的信息公开申请中，这显然背离了该制度最初旨在赋予公民权利的初衷。议员办公室也同样被 AI 撰写的信件所淹没，而工作人员必须逐封阅读，生怕遗漏来自选民的重要诉求。如果公众普及更自动化的 AI 智能体，那么政府机构陷入瘫痪的风险将会进一步加剧。

items.title: PHP 释出更新修复两个允许远程执行代码的高危漏洞
items.content_text:
PHP 项目释出了 PHP 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 和 8.2.35，修复了两个允许未经身份验证远程执行代码的高危漏洞。开发者建议所有 PHP 用户立即进行更新。 CVE-2026-109618(GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w)：内存溢出处理可能会在内部请求数据仅完成部分初始化时中断 PHP；请求清理机制可能会将这些无效数据误认为有效数据进行处理。
CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp)：归属于某个请求的内部状态在其底层内存被释放后仍可能残存。由同一个工作进程处理的后续请求，可能会在正常初始化将其重置之前使用该陈旧状态。

items.title: openEuler 在欧洲推广国产发行版
items.content_text: 在开源欧盟峰会上，推广 Linux 发行版的展位非常少，最显著的是两个中国发行版项目，其中展位最大的是 openEuler。openEuler 是华为 EulerOS 的社区版本，它不再是华为的项目，而是由开放原子开源基金会 （OpenAtom Foundation）托管。开放原子开源基金会成立于 2020 年，其创始成员包括华为、阿里巴巴、百度、腾讯和浪潮等。EulerOS 以及浪潮的 K/UX 最早都是基于 CentOS 项目。而 CentOS 于 2020 年宣布切换到滚动发行版 CentOS Stream。它提供了工具可以将 CentOS 系统迁移到 openEuler。openEuler 采用了类似 Ubuntu 的发布模式，有长期支持版本 LTS，也有短期的版本。它的最新版本是 v26.09，而最近的 LTS 版本是 v24.03，支持开源的 RISC-V 和龙芯的 LoongArch 架构。它的 22.03 LTS 还支持申威处理器 SW-64。

items.title: 联合国报告警告到 2050 年全球升温可能突破 2 °C
items.content_text: 联合国环境规划署发表报告《Emissions Gap Report 2026》，警告除非加快减排步伐，到本世纪中叶全球 升温幅度极有可能突破 2°C。而要将升温峰值控制在 1.7至 1.8°C 之间，则需要本十年末将排放量较 2025 年水平削减 18%，到 2035 年削减 45%，五年后再削减 69%。报告警告称，如果当前政策持续下去，本世纪内全球变暖可能达到 2.8°C，此后还将继续上升。报告指出，由于美国退出气候协议以及对历史排放量的修订估计，这些结果比去年的预测更为严峻。

items.title: The ants are definitely up to something
items.content_text:
Humans-B-Gone! is a labour of love animated series about a society of colossal sapient arthropods where humans are vermin. The series mostly follows a timorous tarantula, a mouthy mantis and the titular pest-control service. Don't worry - there's extensive translation (audio, pheremonal and visual) to make things legible to a human audience. You should thank Professor Gregorsa. Or possibly Rev Storm. With season 1 complete, episode 1 sets the scene, or jump right into the action with Episode 2.

Episodes have substantial unobtrusive footnotes explaining the real-world and in-universe science behind what you've just seen. There's even points to be scored! And don't worry pedants - the square-cube law is in full effect, it simply plays second fiddle to The Unknown Nature. Episodes also available on Newgrounds if you prefer.

items.title: The Adult Children Cleaning Up Their Parents' Feeds
items.content_text: Americans over 60 now spend more than half their leisure hours in front of screens. But unlike millennials and most Gen-Xers, who have spent years navigating engagement bait, stealth marketing, and AI slop — and have developed a working instinct for what to trust — older adults tend to have little idea of what they're looking at. This susceptibility is creating an entirely new type of responsibility for the adult children of these suddenly very online parents, who flock to Reddit to ask things like, How do I stop my dad from watching fake Bruce Lee AI slop? Is it possible to curate a feed for my anxious, elderly mother? and How can I stop my aging parents from believing fake news?

items.title: Every great literary city exists twice

The landmarks have become ordinary, street-side cafés have become just another place to answer emails or meet colleagues after work. Graham Greene's Saigon is no longer the city existing chiefly on the streets outside, but it persists in the habits of mind with which I had learned to walk those streets. The novel is a crucial part of any Westerner's apprenticeship to Vietnam.

The move backfired spectacularly, as numerous Republicans, including Ohio governor Mike DeWine strongly condemned the ad and GOP panic over the race erupted. Even MAGA appears divided. We talked to Jim Swift, a senior editor at The Bulwark, who wrote a good piece on this fiasco. We discuss the deeper reasons Ramaswamy decided this ad would energize the MAGA base, how it could cost Republicans the Ohio gubernatorial and Senate contests, and what this ugly saga says about the depravity of Late-Stage MAGA—and the growing mainstream backlash to it. items.title: Kushner Phone Hack Reveals How Middle East Dictators Bought Him Off
items.content_text:
Jared Kushner oversaw foreign slush funds filled and managed by the leaders of the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Israel, Vanity Fair reported Thursday.

In the forthcoming book Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East, author Matthew Cole made a shocking revelation about Donald Trump’s son-in-law’s potentially illegal dealings with foreign dictators.

During the first Trump administration, the Netherlands Defense Intelligence and Security Service discovered a way to hack into Kushner’s iPhone. Officials learned that he was secretly moving hundreds of thousands of dollars through a bank account at First Dubai Bank.

Crucially, Kushner did not own the account, but was merely a signatory for the account managed and owned by the Watani Al Emarat Foundation, a government-funded charity run by Dherar Belhoul Al Falasi, a close friend of UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, referred to as MBZ.

Starting in 2017, the Saudis and Emiratis transferred roughly $750 million into the account to be used as a foreign policy slush fund. The charity was used to fund the UAE government’s covert intelligence operations overseas, as well as its secret weapons-purchasing programs, one confidential source told Cole.

First Dubai Bank is run by Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, MBZ’s brother. (Tahnoon also oversees a fund called Lunate, which is among the largest stakeholders in Kushner’s shady private equity firm Affinity Partners.) The money was sent by a bank in Azerbaijan, where banks have a well-established but unadvertised practice of exchanging Saudi riyals or Emirati dirhams for an equal amount of American dollars.

Four senior Trump administration officials—including two national security advisers, a White House chief of staff, and a former CIA director—told Cole they were not aware that the president had authorized Kushner to access a foreign government bank account.

Kushner’s lawyer denied that his client had any knowledge of the charity or the bank account, and claimed that Trump’s son-in-law did not make any arrangements with foreign leaders that the president did not agree to.

But that wasn’t the only account Kushner managed. By the spring of 2018, MBZ had also put roughly $1 billion for Kushner into a second account at Israel’s Central Bank—at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s urging. Unlike the political slush fund, Kushner’s activity in this account indicated that it was for his personal use. The money was difficult to access, and so Kushner would channel requests to Netanyahu for the funds to be released through then-Ambassador David M. Friedman, and then move the money through an account in Cyprus. The former diplomat denied any involvement in the scheme, and claimed that “there are no accounts, and never were.”

Additionally, the UAE secretly put money into yet another account at Israel’s Central Bank as a “rainy-day defense fund” in case of an attack from Iran.

It should go without saying, but Kushner did not disclose his access to these accounts to the IRS—potentially violating federal law. At the time, Kushner was a government employee who worked in the White House, meaning he was required to submit both public and confidential financial forms and disclose any bank account on which he had access as a signatory or beneficiary. Kushner also failed to disclose himself as an agent of a foreign government, having been paid nearly $2 billion in total by foreign leaders. If he offered anything in return for the money, even just conversations with his father-in-law, then he would have violated U.S. bribery laws and the foreign agent statute.

This is far from the first time that Kushner has been accused of blatant self-dealing in his service to Trump. He used used peace negotiations with Russia to concoct a multibillion-dollar deal to benefit his business partners, invested in a firm that saw massive gains from Israel’s ongoing military campaign in Gaza, and used his gig as special envoy as an opportunity to try to raise funds from foreign governments and individuals in the Middle East.

items.title: Todd Blanche Floats Chilling Likelihood of Trump Election Interference
items.content_text:
Attorney General Todd Blanche is open to blocking states from certifying the November midterm elections.

Blanche made the comments during a Thursday press gaggle in Virginia.

“Is there any scenario in which DOJ would weigh in on that certification process or try to block states from certifying?” a reporter asked.

“Is there any scenario? Yes,” Blanche said. “Of course there’s scenarios that we could all come up with hypothetically, some doomsday scenario for example, right? I don’t think it’s proper to make any kind of conclusory statements about what’s gonna happen in the future.... It is not DOJ’s intention to—and it’s never our intention—to improperly interfere with our elections.”

“But to say that there’s no circumstances that we would ever do that, of course I’m not gonna say that,” he continued.

The federal government is not supposed to play a role in state certification of elections. The soundbite quickly raised alarm to Blanche’s left.

“THIS IS CODE RED !!” wrote California Governor Gavin Newsom’s press office. “Trump’s politicized DOJ is now saying out loud that they may interfere in the election in a desperate, unprecedented, and completely unAmerican and anti-democratic attempt to keep Trump and MAGA in power.”

“He answered the question of whether Donald Trump’s DOJ may interfere in the midterm elections with a ‘Yes,’” said Campaign for New York Health’s Melanie D’Arrigo.

It is incredibly abnormal for a sitting attorney general to float the possibility of interfering with an election, especially one who believes the Justice Department is not independent from the president (in this case, a president who has spent six years trying to manufacture a baseless voter fraud scandal). Yet Blanche, Trump’s formal personal attorney, did it with ease.

items.title: Rejected Ballots Skyrocketed in Five States Thanks to USPS
items.content_text:
Mail-in ballots are being rejected at a growing rate in rural areas thanks to U.S. Postal Service cuts. 

ProPublica reports that in the primaries this year in Oregon, North Carolina, Washington, California, and Ohio, a staggering amount of ballots arrived too late to be counted due to delays in mail delivery. Three days after primary elections in Stevens County, Washington, election workers checked the mail for late ballots. They found over 500 envelopes when they were only expecting a few dozen. 

The same thing happened in all of eastern Washington’s 11 rural counties. Over 2,000 ballots came in late, compared to just 600 late ballots in 2022’s midterm elections. The nonprofit news outlet traces the issues to a number of changes at the USPS. 

First, over the past three years, the postal service moved to process first-class mail at regional hubs instead of smaller plants closer to local post offices. Then, just after the presidential election two years ago, the USPS cut in half its pickups from post offices at least 50 miles away from those hubs.

That increased delivery time by at least one day. Postmarks, which are critical for legally verifying if a ballot can be counted, were also pushed back as those stamps aren’t added until mail reaches a regional processing center. In rural counties in the five states, late ballots have a grace period as long as they are postmarked by Election Day, but rejections still shot up compared to 2022 according to ProPublica’s findings. 

The postal service’s policy changes were pushed by Trump administration officials, and likely unintentionally hurt the Republican Party.  

“I don’t think they realized how much it was going to affect their voter base,” Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs, a Democrat, told ProPublica, noting that his state has “a lot of rural Republican voters.”

USPS officials claim that delays are much less likely for November’s general election because of “extraordinary measures.” The postal service sent a memo to every post office in the country earlier this fall instructing them to separate ballots from other mail for the 10 days preceding Election Day on November 3. The memo said that the post offices should deliver the ballots on the day they arrive. 

“We work to identify and address issues quickly,” said the chair of the Postal Service board of governors Amber McReynolds in a press conference last week, “so ballots can continue to move swiftly from election offices to voters and from voters back to election offices.”

If they are wrong, though, many races could be affected. A few thousand or even hundred ballots could swing many contests in rural areas, leaving voters across the political spectrum disenfranchised. Trump’s attempts to undermine the entire process aren’t helping, either.

items.title: Van Hollen Demands Answers Over No Kings’ Blocked Accounts
items.content_text:
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen demanded answers Thursday from Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg after the company suspended the No Kings Coalition’s official Instagram account during the group’s nationwide day of action.

In a letter shared exclusively with The New Republic, Van Hollen asked why the coalition’s Instagram was mysteriously shut down for more than an hour during a major day of early voting activations over the weekend. The administrators did not regain access for hours, restricting their ability to communicate with supporters.

Van Hollen asked the MAGA-friendly technocrat whether Meta had communicated internally about the No Kings Coalition, and to explain why it took so long to restore the administrators’ access to the account. So far, Democratic Senators Ron Wyden, Chris Murphy, Richard Blumenthal, and Jeff Merkley have joined Van Hollen’s probe.

Van Hollen also demanded an explanation for Meta’s vacillating excuses for the incident. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone initially claimed Sunday that the account was shut down due to high frequencies of posting, sharing, and commenting. The next day, however, he claimed it had to do with the account’s “reading” behavior.

“Not only are Meta’s shifting explanations alarming, the substance of the claims paint the picture that one of the largest social media companies in the world is somehow incapable of handling technical concerns about an account without shutting it down for hours,” Van Hollen’s letter stated.

The Maryland Democrat also questioned why the account was not included in Meta’s cross-check program, which allows the company to designate civic entities to ensure human review before a decision is made that could severely jeopardize participation in significant political events.

“This is not the first time that Meta has experienced shutdowns or lapses around political speech leading up to the 2026 elections,” the letter stated, referring to a so-called “glitch” that disrupted Ohio Democratic Senate nominee Sherrod Brown’s campaign ads on Facebook and restrictions placed on Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Instagram ahead of his country’s elections. On Tuesday, Meta’s Oversight Board called the incidents part of a series of “recurring enforcement failures in Meta’s election integrity efforts,” and that it was unclear why the error was not caught by the company’s mistake-prevention systems.

“How will you guarantee that accounts sharing critical election and civic information are not incorrectly shutdown in the future? What steps will Meta take between now and election day to ensure that accounts sharing this information are not taken offline without notice?” the letter asked.

With the midterm elections fast-approaching, Van Hollen asked that Zuckerberg provide lawmakers with responses by October 29.

The incident raises serious concerns about Meta’s impartial handling of voting information and political speech—particularly in light of the company’s close financial relationship with the Trump administration. The company awarded nearly $25 million straight into Donald Trump’s pocket, $10 million to a Trump-aligned dark money group, $5 million to the president’s White House ballroom, and $1 million to his inaugural fund. In return, Meta stands to make billions in hefty government contracts and data center handouts.

items.title: Judge Orders Trump to End Election Probe Based on Error-Filled Data
items.content_text:
A judge has ordered the Department of Homeland Security to end its investigations into noncitizen voting in nine states. 

U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín ruled Wednesday that DHS’s data  contains multiple inaccuracies and could be used to target U.S. citizens, The Washington Post reports. She barred the department from using the records in “elections-related field operations and field interviews” but delayed the order, allowing the Trump administration until 5 p.m. Friday to appeal. 

DHS agents have recently been spotted going door to door to look for noncitizen voters. Under the order, DHS would be barred from using the program to continue these operations in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington, and Wisconsin. 

According to the Post, the department built target lists from commercial voter files, official state voter rolls, and other lists comprising 48.2 million voters that Martínez-Olguín, appointed by President Biden, said came from “questionable provenance.”

Because of pressure from administration officials, DHS employees were only given up to 12 minutes to clear someone from the list, Martínez-Olguín said. She ruled that this had a high likelihood of error because the government doesn’t keep a true master list of people living in the U.S. that includes their citizenship status. 

Groups including the California Nurses Association sued the government, claiming that the White House was violating the Voting Rights Act by intimidating people who try to increase voter turnout or help with voting. Martínez-Olguín ruled that these groups had valid claims. 

“The fear is objectively reasonable, and compounded by [DHS’s] use of data that is widely known to inadvertently include U.S. citizens, leaves citizens afraid that their name will be wrongly included in the hundreds of thousands identified for investigation,” Martínez-Olguín wrote. 

Earlier this week, the Department of Justice admitted that its list of noncitizens who illegally voted in California may not be accurate, and officials in the state as well as Los Angeles County attested the same in court. That hasn’t stopped the federal government from arresting people based on that faulty information, though.

items.title: AI Bots Are Accessing People’s Bank Accounts Unprompted
items.content_text:
Major American banks have reported unauthorized artificial intelligence bots inside consumer accounts, sources told Axios Thursday.

The infiltration is happening faster than the financial institutions can respond to it. Even more concerning, some of the agents appear to be acting independently, performing actions that users did not request or automate.

Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo are just some of the banks racing to contain the AI-related risk. Part of the containment strategy involves rapidly rewriting and redeploying terms of service to their clients in order to firmly restrict the use of AI from their platforms.

Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citi are in the process of restricting third-party agents from accessing their platforms entirely, according to Axios.

Bank executives described the situation to Axios as “horrifying.” One official told the digital newsroom that the industry has “grave concerns” about whether the rampant threat could impact user finances.

Executives reportedly recognize that a growing demographic of banking clients are interested in using their own AI agents to perform financial tasks and transactions. However, the risk is currently too high to allow individual clients that kind of access, particularly at the rate at which the revolutionary technology is adapting and changing.

Another banking executive told Axios that it is difficult to distinguish between authorized AI agents and agents that have “gone rogue” and inappropriately accessed a customer account.

“Banks are investing in preventing worst-case scenarios, but they are also preparing in case they do happen, including with ‘day after’ scenario planning that would allow them to quickly secure or restore customer access,” Axios reported.

items.title: State Department Unveils Plan to Only Promote Trump Supporters
items.content_text:
The Department of State has asked civil servants up for promotions who they voted for in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 presidential elections.
